11. Getting Started

Quick checklist for deploying your custom pool:

  1. Define token list: Which tokens to support?
  2. Configure risk: What coverage ratios, decay rates?
  3. Design hooks: Any custom deposit bonuses, fees, incentives?
  4. Deploy: Use provided factory or deploy directly
  5. Customize UI: Point to your pool address, theme your interface
  6. Launch: Market to your users
  7. (Optional) Partner: Contact team for strategic collaborations

No approval required — permissionless by design.

1.3.2-hooks.title: 1.3.2. Hooks
1.3.2-hooks.html:
Pool Hooks System

Overview

The Pool Hooks System provides a gas-efficient, runtime-updateable mechanism for extending pool functionality through custom logic at key lifecycle points. Hooks enable per-token customization without modifying core pool logic.

Design Philosophy

  • Minimal: Direct inline calls, zero runtime validation overhead
  • Updateable: Owner can swap hook contracts without liquidity migration
  • Token-Centric: One hook contract per asset, finest granularity of customization
  • Type-Safe: ERC-165 interface detection and compile-time selector validation
  • Gas-Efficient: Flagged executiononly call hooks that are actually implemented

Hook Interface

Complete IPoolHooks Interface (12 Functions)

interface IPoolHooks {
    // POOL INITIALIZATION (2 hooks)
    function preInitialize(address pool, address owner, address baseToken, address wnative) external;
    function postInitialize(address pool, address owner, address baseToken, address wnative) external;
 
    // DEPOSITS (2 hooks)
    function preDeposit(address pool, address sender, address token, uint256 amountIn) external;
    function postDeposit(
        address pool, address sender, address token, uint256 amountIn, uint256 lpMinted
    ) external returns (uint256 hookFeeOut, uint256 hookIncentiveOut);
 
    // WITHDRAWALS (2 hooks)
    function preWithdraw(address pool, address sender, address token, uint256 lpAmount) external;
    function postWithdraw(
        address pool, address sender, address token, uint256 amountOutGross, uint256 lpBurned
    ) external returns (uint256 exitFee, uint256 incentiveOut);
 
    // SWAPS (2 hooks)
    function preSwap(
        address pool, address sender, address tokenIn, address tokenOut,
        uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutQuoted
    ) external returns (uint256 extraFeeOut, uint16 newFeeBps);
 
    function postSwap(
        address pool, address sender, address tokenIn, address tokenOut,
        uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutFinal
    ) external returns (int256 hookDeltaOut);
 
    // DONATIONS (2 hooks)
    function preDonate(address pool, address sender, address token, uint256 amount) external;
    function postDonate(address pool, address sender, address token, uint256 amount) external;
 
    // FLASH LOANS (2 hooks)
    function preFlashLoan(
        address pool, address initiator, address token, uint256 amount, uint256 fee, bytes calldata data
    ) external;
    function postFlashLoan(
        address pool, address initiator, address token, uint256 amount, uint256 fee, bytes calldata data
    ) external;
 
    /// @notice Returns bitmask of implemented hooks (gas optimization)
    /// @return uint32 with bits set for each implemented hook
    function hookFlags() external pure returns (uint32);
}

Key Features:

  • 12 lifecycle hooks covering: initialization, deposits, withdrawals, swaps, donations, flash loans
  • Hook flags bitmask for gas optimization (specify which hooks the contract implements)
  • Return values enable hooks to dynamically adjust pool behavior:
    • postDeposit/postWithdraw: Add/remove LP fees or incentives
    • preSwap: Override fees or add extra charges
    • postSwap: Adjust final pool reserves with signed delta

Hook Semantics

All hooks follow pool perspective semantics (how the pool views the operation):

Hook Pool Action User Action Use Case
preDeposit RECEIVES liquidity Deposits tokens Validate whitelist, check position limits
postDeposit RECEIVED liquidity Deposited tokens Deploy to yield (Aave, Morpho), update accounting
preWithdraw GIVES liquidity back Withdraws Prepare withdrawal, check position state
postWithdraw GAVE liquidity back Withdrew Apply exit fees, rebalance reserves
preSwap EXCHANGES tokens Swaps Override fees, add extra charges
postSwap EXCHANGED tokens Completed swap Adjust reserves with delta, rebalance
preDonate RECEIVES donation Donates tokens Validate donor, check limits
postDonate RECEIVED donation Completed donation Accounting updates, redistribute yield
preFlashLoan LENDS token Borrows Validate borrower, check risk
postFlashLoan RECEIVED repayment Repaid loan Rebalance, update accounting

Example: User swaps USDC → BTC

  • Pool RECEIVES USDC (buys): preSwap(USDC) + postSwap(USDC)
  • Pool GIVES BTC (sells): preSwap(BTC) + postSwap(BTC)
  • Both tokens' hooks are called, enabling per-token custom logic

Hook Storage & Registry

Storage Model

mapping(address => address) hooks;       // Per-asset hook contract
mapping(address => uint32) hookFlags;    // Per-asset: bitmask of implemented hooks

Architecture:

  • One hook contract per asset (not per-pool or per-pair)
  • Single contract implements all 12 hook functions and routes based on token parameter
  • Hook flags enable gas optimization: unset flags = hook not called

Hook Flags Constants

uint32 constant HOOK_PRE_INIT = 1 << 0;          // Bit 0
uint32 constant HOOK_POST_INIT = 1 << 1;         // Bit 1
uint32 constant HOOK_PRE_DEPOSIT = 1 << 2;       // Bit 2
uint32 constant HOOK_POST_DEPOSIT = 1 << 3;      // Bit 3
uint32 constant HOOK_PRE_WITHDRAW = 1 << 4;      // Bit 4
uint32 constant HOOK_POST_WITHDRAW = 1 << 5;     // Bit 5
uint32 constant HOOK_PRE_SWAP = 1 << 6;          // Bit 6
uint32 constant HOOK_POST_SWAP = 1 << 7;         // Bit 7
uint32 constant HOOK_PRE_DONATE = 1 << 8;        // Bit 8
uint32 constant HOOK_POST_DONATE = 1 << 9;       // Bit 9
uint32 constant HOOK_PRE_FLASH_LOAN = 1 << 10;   // Bit 10
uint32 constant HOOK_POST_FLASH_LOAN = 1 << 11;  // Bit 11

Usage Pattern:

function _hook(address token, uint32 flag) internal view returns (address h) {
    h = hooks[token];
    if (h == address(0)) return address(0);
    return (hookFlags[token] & flag) != 0 ? h : address(0);
}
 
// Only call hook if flag is set
address hook = _hook(token, HOOK_PRE_DEPOSIT);
if (hook != address(0)) {
    IPoolHooks(hook).preDeposit(address(this), msg.sender, token, amount);
}

Hook Execution Flow

Deposits

1. preDeposit (if HOOK_PRE_DEPOSIT flag set)
   � Validate whitelist, check position limits, etc.
 
2. Transfer tokens in
   � Pull user's tokens to pool
 
3. Mint LP tokens
   � Calculate LP amount based on asset index
 
4. postDeposit (if HOOK_POST_DEPOSIT flag set)
   � Returns: (hookFeeOut, hookIncentiveOut)
   � Example: deposit 100 USDC to Aave, return 0 fee, 0 incentive
   � Final LP = lpAmount + hookIncentiveOut - hookFeeOut

Example: Aave Yield Hook

  • postDeposit: Supplies new deposit to Aave (receives aToken)
  • Aave hook manages aToken balance as part of reserves
  • Coverage haircut naturally applies to aToken positions

Withdrawals

1. preWithdraw (if HOOK_PRE_WITHDRAW flag set)
   � Prepare withdrawal (e.g., withdraw from Aave if needed)
 
2. Calculate withdrawal amount
   � Apply coverage ratio haircut
   � Check sufficient reserves
 
3. Burn LP tokens
 
4. postWithdraw (if HOOK_POST_WITHDRAW flag set)
   � Returns: (exitFee, incentiveOut)
   � Example: collect 1% exit fee
   � Final withdrawal = amountOut + incentiveOut - exitFee

Swaps

1. preSwap (BOTH tokenIn and tokenOut hooks, if HOOK_PRE_SWAP set)
   � Hook on tokenIn returns: (extraFeeOut, newFeeBps)
   � Hook on tokenOut returns: (extraFeeOut, newFeeBps)
   � Use fee override if both specify same fee
 
2. Execute swap
   � Calculate amountOut (accounting for fees)
   � Verify slippage protection
   � Update reserves
 
3. postSwap (BOTH tokenIn and tokenOut hooks, if HOOK_POST_SWAP set)
   � Hook on tokenIn returns: int256 delta
   � Hook on tokenOut returns: int256 delta
   � Adjust final reserves: (delta > 0) = pool receives, (delta < 0) = pool gives

Example: Multi-Hook Swap

  • USDC hook (Aave): preSwap withdraws from Aave, postSwap re-deposits excess
  • WETH hook (Whitelist): preSwap checks sender, postSwap updates position tracking

Flash Loans

1. preFlashLoan (if HOOK_PRE_FLASH_LOAN set)
   � Validate borrower, check risk limits
 
2. Lend tokens to borrower
   � Borrower executes callback logic
 
3. Collect fee and repayment
 
4. postFlashLoan (if HOOK_POST_FLASH_LOAN set)
   � Rebalance reserves, update accounting

Hook Implementation Examples

Base Hook Template

All hooks should inherit from a base contract that implements the pool interface:

contract MyPoolHook is IPoolHooks {
    address public immutable pool;
 
    constructor(address _pool) {
        pool = _pool;
    }
 
    modifier onlyPool() {
        require(msg.sender == pool, "Only pool");
        _;
    }
 
    function preDeposit(address, address, address, uint256) external onlyPool {}
    function postDeposit(address, address, address, uint256, uint256)
        external onlyPool returns (uint256, uint256)
    {
        return (0, 0); // No fee, no incentive
    }
 
    // ... implement all 12 hooks ...
 
    function hookFlags() external pure returns (uint32) {
        // Set bits for hooks this contract actually implements
        return (1 << 2) | (1 << 3);  // HOOK_PRE_DEPOSIT | HOOK_POST_DEPOSIT
    }
}

Example 1: Aave Yield Optimization

Automatically deposits reserves to Aave and withdraws when needed:

contract AaveYieldHook is IPoolHooks {
    address public immutable pool;
    IPool public immutable aavePool;
    address public owner;
 
    constructor(address _pool, address _aavePool, address _owner) {
        pool = _pool;
        aavePool = _aavePool;
        owner = _owner;
    }
 
    mapping(address => bool) public yieldEnabled;  // Per-token config
    mapping(address => uint8) public bufferPercent; // Keep 10% in pool
 
    function postDeposit(address, address, address token, uint256 depositAmount, uint256)
        external returns (uint256, uint256)
    {
        if (!yieldEnabled[token]) return (0, 0);
 
        // Keep buffer in pool, deposit rest to Aave
        uint256 toDeposit = (depositAmount * (100 - bufferPercent[token])) / 100;
        IERC20(token).approve(address(aavePool), toDeposit);
        aavePool.supply(token, toDeposit, address(this), 0);
 
        return (0, 0); // No fee/incentive
    }
 
    function preBuy(address, address, address token, uint256, uint256, bytes calldata)
        external
    {
        // Called when pool BUYS token (receives it from swapper)
        // If low on balance, withdraw from Aave
        uint256 balance = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this));
        if (balance < someMinimum) {
            uint256 toWithdraw = (depositAmount * (100 - bufferPercent[token])) / 100;
            aavePool.withdraw(token, toWithdraw, address(this));
        }
    }
 
    function postBuy(address, address, address token, uint256, uint256, bytes calldata)
        external
    {
        // Re-deposit excess to Aave after receiving
        uint256 excess = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this));
        if (excess > bufferAmount) {
            uint256 toDeposit = excess - bufferAmount;
            IERC20(token).approve(address(aavePool), toDeposit);
            aavePool.supply(token, toDeposit, address(this), 0);
        }
    }
 
    function hookFlags() external pure returns (uint32) {
        return (1 << 3) | (1 << 6) | (1 << 7);  // POST_DEPOSIT | PRE_SWAP | POST_SWAP
    }
}

Example 2: Whitelist with Position Limits

Restrict deposits to whitelisted addresses with per-user position limits:

contract WhitelistHook is IPoolHooks {
    address public immutable pool;
    address public owner;
 
    mapping(address => mapping(address => bool)) public whitelisted; // pool → token → user → allowed
    mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public positionLimits; // token → user → max LP
    mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public userPositions; // token → user → current LP
 
    function preDeposit(address, address depositor, address token, uint256) external {
        require(whitelisted[address(this)][depositor], "Not whitelisted");
    }
 
    function postDeposit(address, address depositor, address token, uint256, uint256 lpMinted)
        external returns (uint256, uint256)
    {
        uint256 newPosition = userPositions[token][depositor] + lpMinted;
        uint256 limit = positionLimits[token][depositor];
        require(newPosition <= limit, "Position limit exceeded");
 
        userPositions[token][depositor] = newPosition;
        return (0, 0);
    }
 
    function postWithdraw(address, address withdrawer, address token, uint256, uint256 lpBurned)
        external returns (uint256, uint256)
    {
        userPositions[token][withdrawer] -= lpBurned;
        return (0, 0); // No exit fees
    }
 
    function hookFlags() external pure returns (uint32) {
        return (1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 5);  // PRE_DEPOSIT | POST_DEPOSIT | POST_WITHDRAW
    }
 
    // Admin functions
    function addToWhitelist(address token, address user) external {
        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only owner");
        whitelisted[address(this)][user] = true;
    }
 
    function setPositionLimit(address token, address user, uint256 limit) external {
        require(msg.sender == owner, "Only owner");
        positionLimits[token][user] = limit;
    }
}

Example 3: Deposit-Only Hook

Demonstrate hook flags optimizationonly implement deposit hooks, all other hooks are no-ops:

contract DepositOnlyHook is IPoolHooks {
    address public immutable pool;
 
    function preDeposit(address, address, address token, uint256 amount) external {
        // Custom deposit validation
        require(amount > 0, "Invalid amount");
    }
 
    function postDeposit(address, address, address, uint256, uint256)
        external returns (uint256, uint256)
    {
        // Custom deposit logic
        return (0, 0);
    }
 
    // All other hooks: no implementation needed
 
    function hookFlags() external pure returns (uint32) {
        // Only these two hooks are called
        return (1 << 2) | (1 << 3);  // HOOK_PRE_DEPOSIT | HOOK_POST_DEPOSIT
    }
}

All other hooks automatically become no-ops due to flag checking in pool core:

// In pool core:
address hook = _hook(token, HOOK_PRE_WITHDRAW);
if (hook != address(0)) {  // This is false because flag not set
    IPoolHooks(hook).preWithdraw(...);
}

Hook Registration & Validation

Registration Flow

function updateHooks(address token, address hookAddress) external onlyOwner {
    // Validate hook contract if not disabling
    if (hookAddress != address(0)) {
        _validateHookContract(hookAddress);
    }
 
    hooks[token] = hookAddress;
    emit HooksUpdated(token, hookAddress);
}

Validation Strategy

Comprehensive one-time validation at registration (not runtime):

  1. Code check: Ensure address has contract code (not EOA)
  2. ERC-165 support: Verify supportsInterface(IPoolHooks) returns true
  3. Selector validation: Call all 12 hooks with dummy data, verify correct return values

Benefits:

  • Zero runtime validation overhead (~2k gas saved per operation)
  • All hooks guaranteed compliant before use
  • Early detection of invalid hooks (rejected before use)
  • Owner can instantly replace hooks via updateHooks(token, newHook)

Disabling Hooks

To disable hooks for a token:

bamm.updateHooks(token, address(0));
// Now: only ~100 gas overhead (address check) on operations

Security Considerations

Protected Against

 Reentrancy: Hooks called within pool's nonReentrant context  Invalid Hooks: Comprehensive validation at registration (all 12 hooks tested)  Unauthorized Access: Hook contracts implement onlyPool modifier  Bypass Attacks: Hook reverts cause full transaction revert  Upgrade Risks: Instant rollback possible via updateHooks(token, oldHook)  Gas Griefing: No runtime validation (validated once at registration)  Return Value Attacks: Selector validation ensures correct return types

Hook Access Control

All hook contracts MUST implement access control:

modifier onlyPool() {
    require(msg.sender == pool, "Only pool");
    _;
}
 
function preDeposit(...) external onlyPool {
    // Logic
}

Without this, anyone could call hooks and manipulate pool state.

Return Value Semantics

Hooks must respect return value contracts:

Hook Return Type Purpose
postDeposit (uint256 fee, uint256 incentive) Adjust final LP amount
postWithdraw (uint256 fee, uint256 incentive) Adjust final withdrawal
preSwap (uint256 extraFee, uint16 feeOverride) Modify swap fees
postSwap int256 delta Adjust pool reserves
hookFlags uint32 Bitmask of implemented hooks
Other hooks void No return value

Incorrect return values or types = hook will fail validation.

Gas Costs

Operation Hook Disabled Hook Enabled (no-op) Hook Enabled (Aave)
Deposit ~100 gas ~5,000 gas ~55,000 gas
Withdraw ~100 gas ~5,000 gas ~60,000 gas
Swap ~200 gas ~10,000 gas ~110,000 gas
Flash Loan ~100 gas ~5,000 gas ~50,000 gas

Cost Breakdown

  • Disabled hooks: Just address check (hooks[token] != address(0))
  • Enabled hooks (no-op): Function call overhead (~5k gas)
  • Enabled hooks (real logic): Function call + custom logic (varies)
  • Registration: ~100-200k gas (one-time, validates all 12 hooks)

Optimization Strategies

  1. Hook Flags: Only set bits for hooks you actually use

    // DepositOnlyHook: FLAGS = 0x0C (bits 2-3)
// Saves gas on all non-deposit operations

  2. Conditional Logic: Route per-token inside single hook

    function postDeposit(address, address, address token, uint256 amount, uint256)
    external returns (uint256, uint256)
{
    if (token == usdc) {
        // USDC-specific (expensive)
    } else if (token == dai) {
        // DAI-specific (cheap)
    }
}

  3. Selective Token Hooks: Disable hooks on low-value tokens

    updateHooks(dai, address(0));      // Disable: ~100 gas overhead
updateHooks(usdc, aaveHook);       // Enable: Aave yield optimization

Best Practices

1. Hook Design

  • Single Responsibility: One hook contract per use case

    // Bad: mixing Aave, whitelist, fee logic
contract MixedHook { ... }
 
// Good: separate hooks
contract AaveHook { ... }
contract WhitelistHook { ... }
contract FeeHook { ... }

  • Token-Centric Routing: Handle multiple tokens inside single hook

    function postDeposit(address, address, address token, uint256 amount, uint256)
    external returns (uint256, uint256)
{
    if (token == usdc) { /* Aave */ }
    else if (token == weth) { /* Whitelist */ }
    else if (token == dai) { /* Fee */ }
}

  • Minimal Return Values: Only return non-zero for necessary adjustments

    // Most hooks return (0, 0) or 0
// Only postDeposit/postWithdraw return fees/incentives if needed

2. Integration

  • Pre-Hook Validation: Validate state before core operation
  • Post-Hook Adjustment: Modify results after core operation
  • Error Handling: Let hook reverts propagate (fail-safe model)

3. Testing

  • Deploy hook with desired configuration
  • Test each hook independently with dummy data
  • Test hook registration validation
  • Test hook disable and re-enable
  • Profile gas costs (enabled vs disabled)
  • Test per-token routing if applicable
  • Test return value semantics
  • Test reentrancy protection
  • Verify access control (onlyPool modifier)

4. Maintenance

  • Version Control: Tag hook versions (v1, v2, etc.)
  • Deployment Records: Keep audit trail of hook updates
  • Instant Rollback: Keep old hook contract deployed for quick revert
    // If v2 has issues:
updateHooks(token, v1_address);  // Instant rollback, no LP migration

Troubleshooting

Problem Diagnosis Solution
Hook not being called Check hookFlags[token] has bit set Set correct bit for hook
Hook returns wrong type Return value mismatch Verify return type matches interface
Hook reverts on valid input Logic error in hook Debug hook contract in isolation
High gas on operations Hook doing too much work Profile hook execution, optimize
Can't update hook Validation failed Ensure hook implements all 12 functions with correct selectors

Summary

The Pool Hooks System combines:

 Per-Token Customization - Finest granularity (one hook per asset)  Runtime Updateability - Swap hook contracts without liquidity migration  Gas Efficiency - Flag-based execution, ~100 gas when disabled  Type Safety - ERC-165 interface detection, selector validation  Security - One-time registration validation, zero runtime overhead  Simplicity - Direct calls, clear pool-perspective semantics

Best For: Protocols needing per-token custom logic (yield optimization, access control, dynamic fees) with ability to upgrade over time.

Key Files & References

File Purpose
contracts/src/interfaces/IPoolHooks.sol IPoolHooks interface definition
contracts/src/libraries/LibConstants.sol Hook flag constants
contracts/src/modules/BaseV1.sol _hook() helper for flag checking
contracts/src/modules/CoreV1.sol Hook execution in deposits, withdrawals, swaps
old/contracts/hooks/*.sol Example hook implementations
